The refuter was correct. The old Klein-four witness paired the diagonal subgroup with the wrong quotient map, so it was not a short exact sequence at all. The current counterexample uses two honest Z/9 extensions of C_3 by C_3 with the same middle group and incompatible kernel/quotient data.

The refuter was correct. The old definition mentioned nonabelian H^1_nab(N,M) without ever introducing M as a G-group. The current definition types that last sentence explicitly by adding the needed G-group hypothesis on M.

The refuter was correct. The old refutation used the same broken Klein-four witness as the companion counterexample. The current false statement is now refuted by the explicit pair of Z/9 extensions whose middle groups agree but whose kernel/quotient data cannot be matched by an automorphism.

The refuter was correct. The old step 3.2 treated H and K as complements to A even though A already lay inside both groups. The current proof instead passes to G/A and concludes H=K directly from H/A=K/A because A is normal and contained in both complements.

The refuter was correct. The old theorem falsely claimed that a kernel retraction is equivalent to splitting. The current statement narrows the equivalence to split, complement, and semidirect-product data, and states separately that a kernel retraction forces a direct-product splitting.

The refuter was correct. The old contradiction used the nonexistent quotient Z_q/pZ_q for q not equal p. The current refutation uses the actual finite quotient Z_q/qZ_q isomorphic to Z/qZ from the q-adic factor.

The refuter was correct. The old false statement asserted that the finitely generated Frattini formula was itself false. The current item is repaired to the mathematically correct theorem that Phi(G)=[G,G]G^p in this pro-p setting, with the cited literature fact made explicit.

The refuter was correct. The old maximality argument claimed N was not contained in H without proving it. The current proof instead treats HN as a proper open overgroup of H and rules out HN=G via the contradiction xN intersect H empty.

The refuter was correct. The old statement omitted the characteristic-p hypothesis needed for the vertex theory. The current statement now fixes a field k of characteristic p and a finite-dimensional kG-module.

The refuter was correct. The old proof chose a minimal p-subgroup without first showing relative projectivity for any p-subgroup. The current proof starts from a maximal p-subgroup P and uses the Higman trace with [G:P]^{-1} to produce relative P-projectivity before minimizing.

The refuter was correct. The old metric comparison used the strict inequality d_p less than p^{-n}, which misses the case where the first disagreement occurs at coordinate n+1. The current proof uses the exact closed ball d_p less-than-or-equal p^{-n}.

The refuter was correct. The old converse chose a maximal left ideal avoiding a vector t without any reason that t survived modulo every maximal ideal. The current proof instead passes to the cyclic submodule generated by t, takes a maximal submodule there, and produces the nontrivial simple quotient directly.

The refuter was correct. The old proof concluded that the two comparison maps f and g were inverse maps once gf and fg were bijective. The current proof only uses those bijectivities to show f is itself an isomorphism, which is the statement actually needed.

The refuter was correct. The old facts block dropped the Axiom of Choice hypothesis from the cited inverse-limit compactness theorem. The current statement and Given line now carry the Choice boundary exactly where compactness is claimed.

The refuter was correct. The old convergence step repeated the same off-by-one metric inequality as the topology theorem. The current proof uses d_p less-than-or-equal p^{-n} and then chooses n with p^{-n} less than epsilon.
